title: Martha Pomelo (NSIC Pm 01): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Martha Pomelo: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Martha pomelo is a pomelo variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Martha is a registered pomelo variety, also sold or known as NSIC Pm 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1996 as NSIC 1996 Pm 01. Cornelio Maligalig bred it. Its record notes a yield of 50 to 60 fruits/cropping.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Pm 01, this is the same pomelo. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [pomelo variety finder](/crop-varieties/pomelo), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [fertilizer for fruit trees](/blog/fertilizer-for-fruit-trees).

items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of 50 to 60 fruits/cropping.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Martha was about 18 years old and about 5 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 50 to 60 fruits/cropping. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit pomelo fields most often: [citrus greening](/diseases/citrus-greening), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

Why farmers know it: the first pomelo on the NSIC list, a Leyte farmer's selection. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Martha pomelo

Davao is the home of suha. Pick a registered selection by flesh color and sweetness, and plant marcotted trees. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Pm 01 the same as Martha?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Pm 01 is another name for Martha, registered as NSIC 1996 Pm 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 50 to 60 fruits/cropping. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Martha?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
